text:
PyTorch generates map-style sampler indices in the main process; dataset fetching and collation execute in workers. Prefetching advances production ahead of consumption, so sampler progress or worker-side logs cannot identify exactly which batches trained the model. Persistent workers retain dataset instances across epochs. Worker seeds derive from a base seed; iterator creation can consume RNG state, and a supplied generator controls RandomSampler and worker base seeds. Consequently, adding diagnostic iterations or changing generator wiring can alter an existing training sequence. [PyTorch data-loading documentation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/data.md), [DataLoader implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/utils/data/dataloader.py).

Implementation recommendation inferred from these mechanics: capture batches in the main training loop after all stochastic masking/sampling and immediately before model use. Store detached CPU clones of the exact `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors, preserving order and recording step numbers. Avoid extra iterator creation, sampler calls, or RNG draws; worker-local dataset attributes will not reliably expose traces to the parent. Provide a replay iterable over the captured tensors to the unchanged `DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` interface. Mark bounded traces as subsets of consumed batches. This records actual inputs without reconstructing prefetched worker state; preserve existing ordering settings because unordered delivery can make timing relevant. [DataLoader implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/utils/data/dataloader.py).

Exact restart is a separate problem: TorchData’s StatefulDataLoader supports loader checkpoints and aggregates worker state, with custom dataset/sampler state hooks. Saving only the main-process RNG or sampler cursor is insufficient to reproduce stochastic worker transformations. [StatefulDataLoader documentation](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/data/blob/main/torchdata/stateful_dataloader/README.md).
